entries.title: How did the Nineteenth Amendment change voting?
entries.answer: The Nineteenth Amendment says that a U.S. citizen’s right to vote cannot be denied because of their sex. In the years before 1920, some states already allowed women to vote in some or all elections, while others did not. After years of organizing and debate, enough states approved the amendment in 1920 for it to take effect across the country. People still faced other unfair barriers to voting. For instance, officials in some states continued to use racist rules and practices to turn Black citizens away.

sections.heading: A word for the right to vote
sections.text: Suffrage means the right to vote in political elections. People who worked for women’s suffrage organized meetings, wrote to leaders, and marched.

facts: Tennessee was the state whose approval in 1920 brought the amendment to the number required.
An amendment is an official change or addition to the Constitution.

entries.title: What did the Declaration of Independence say?
entries.answer: In 1776, the Continental Congress approved a document saying that 13 British colonies in North America were separating from Great Britain. The Declaration of Independence explained why they were taking that step and described rights they said people should have. The war with Britain was already underway. The ideas in the document went farther than what the new country put into practice at the time. For example, slavery continued even after the leaders said that people were equal.

sections.heading: Two dates
sections.text: Congress adopted the text on July 4, 1776. Delegates began signing the large copy now at the National Archives on August 2. Some signed later.

facts: The document announced independence before the Revolutionary War ended.
The Declaration is preserved at the National Archives.

entries.title: Why was Yellowstone made a national park?
entries.answer: Yellowstone became a national park in 1872. An important reason was that people wanted to keep its geysers, hot springs, and other unusual natural features protected and open to visitors. A geyser can send a burst of steam and water up from the ground. One famous geyser, Old Faithful, has drawn visitors for many years. Yellowstone also includes rivers, forests, and habitat for wildlife. Most of the park is in Wyoming, with parts in Montana and Idaho.

sections.heading: How to look
sections.text: At Yellowstone’s hot areas, visitors stay on boardwalks and other marked paths. Even ground that looks solid can be hot and unsafe.

facts: Yellowstone opened as the first U.S. national park.
It was set aside by a law passed by Congress and signed in 1872.
